questions.prompt: What should an OpenAPI description document for an operation?
options: Its path and method, parameters, request and response schemas, security needs, and relevant response codes.
Only a title and a screenshot of the response.
Private keys, production tokens, or live customer records to make examples realistic.
Only the success status while leaving authentication and validation undocumented.
questions.answer_key: Its path and method, parameters, request and response schemas, security needs, and relevant response codes.
questions.explanation: Its path and method, parameters, request and response schemas, security needs, and relevant response codes. This is especially relevant to “API Documentation Interfaces” because the API contract must remain explicit and reviewable.

questions.prompt: For the lesson “API Documentation Interfaces”, which check provides the strongest practical evidence?
options: Rely on a code review comment without running any representative check.
Run one happy-path call and skip invalid, denied, and failure scenarios.
Test against production records so the exercise cannot be repeated safely.
Validate the OpenAPI document and compare its declared contract with observed responses.
questions.answer_key: Validate the OpenAPI document and compare its declared contract with observed responses.
questions.explanation: A useful check is repeatable, tied to an observable contract, and includes an important negative or boundary scenario.

questions.prompt: Which review warning is most relevant to “API Documentation Interfaces”?
options: A representative test can reproduce the result.
The API avoids exposing internal secrets and personal data.
The specification disagrees with the implementation or omits security and error behavior.
The expected behavior and relevant failure cases are documented.
questions.answer_key: The specification disagrees with the implementation or omits security and error behavior.
questions.explanation: This finding weakens a core API guarantee and should be treated as a design or release issue, not only a style concern.
